st.2: Bhagwanpura is in Hisar district.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhagwanpura is in Kurukshetra district, not Hisar.

st.4: No lion is shown among the animals around the figure.

x: All four statements are correct: the seated figure is ringed by an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros and a buffalo, with two deer below, and no lion appears; the steatite seal comes from Mohenjodaro.

st.2: It is written in Prakrit in the Kharosthi script.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the inscription is in Prakrit but in the Brahmi script, not Kharosthi.

st.1: They include dates from Sivagalai in Thoothukudi district.

x: Both statements are correct: the dates come from Tamil Nadu sites such as Sivagalai and suggest iron use began much earlier than the Gangetic date of about 1000 BCE.

st.3: Even with them, the Later Vedic king had no standing army.

x: All three statements are correct: the twelve Ratnins were royal functionaries honoured in the Ratnahavimshi rite of the Rajasuya, and the Later Vedic king still had no standing army.

st.2: Its full description is found in the Aitareya Brahmana.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the full description of the Upanayana is in the Shatapatha Brahmana, not the Aitareya Brahmana.

st.2: Dharma Sutras deal with the measurement of altars.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the measurement of altars is the subject of the Sulbasutras; Dharma Sutras deal with law and duty.

st.2: The Dakshinapatha was the route from the Ganga valley to the Deccan.

x: All three statements are correct: the Uttarapatha ran from Taxila to Tamralipti, the Dakshinapatha led south to the Deccan, and Kotilingala, Dhulikatta and Kondapur were Satavahana centres.
Both statements are correct: the Satavahanas first used inherited punch-marked coins, and Yajnasri Satakarni issued the ship-mast coins.

st.3: The Buddha nominated Ananda as head of the Sangha after his death.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Buddha named no successor, not even Ananda; the Dhamma and Vinaya were to guide the Sangha.

st.3: The early relic stupa of Jaggayyapeta lies on the bank of the Godavari.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Jaggayyapeta lies on the Krishna, not the Godavari.

st.4: Odisha's Buddhist 'Diamond Triangle' is made up of Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Dhauli.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Diamond Triangle is Ratnagiri, Udayagiri and Lalitgiri, not Dhauli.

st.3: The Third Buddhist Council and the Ceylon mission came after the Kalinga War.

x: All three statements are correct: after Kalinga, Bherighosha gave way to Dhammaghosha, Dhammavijaya replaced conquest, and the Third Council and the Ceylon mission followed the war.

st.3: Antiochus III took tribute from Subhagasena after crossing the Hindu Kush.

x: All three statements are correct: Samprati patronised Jainism, the western half passed from Kunala to Samprati until the Indo-Greeks, and Antiochus III took tribute from Subhagasena.

st.2: Yaksha and Yakshi statues belong to the popular art of the Mauryas.
st.4: The Kanaganahalli slab of Ashoka is a Mauryan work.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the Kanaganahalli slab showing Ashoka is a later Satavahana-period relief, not a Mauryan work.

st.2: Under Skandagupta the lake was repaired by his governor Parnadatta.
st.3: Motupalli and Koduru served South-East Asian trade under the Ikshvakus.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Motupalli and Koduru served South-East Asian trade under the Vishnukundins, not the Ikshvakus.

st.3: Zero reached Europe from Indian mathematics through the Arabs.

x: All three statements are correct: Aryabhata used zero and place value, Brahmagupta gave the rules for zero, and the Indian zero reached Europe through the Arabs.

st.2: The Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam was built by the Sailendra king Sri Mara Vijayottungavarman with Rajaraja I's permission.

x: All three statements are correct: Sastri's 'Chola lake', the Sailendra-built Chudamani Vihara at Nagapattinam, and the Cholas' overseas naval campaigns.

st.3: The last Chalukya-Chola ruler in Vengi was Rajaraja Chola Ganga.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the last Chalukya-Chola ruler in Vengi was Parantaka Chola; Rajaraja Chola Ganga was an earlier viceroy.

st.2: The Maldives were conquered by Rajendra I.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Maldives were conquered by Rajaraja I, not Rajendra I.

st.2: The First Ilbari line was founded by Iltutmish.

x: All three statements are correct: Aibak founded the Qutbi line, Iltutmish the First Ilbari line and Balban the Second Ilbari line.

st.1: He was the uncle of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Firoz Shah was the cousin, not the uncle, of Muhammad bin Tughlaq.

st.1: Khalisa was the land assigned to army commanders.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: khalisa was crown land whose revenue went to the royal treasury, not land assigned to commanders.

st.3: Brahmins remained exempt throughout the Sultanate.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Brahmins were not exempt throughout; Firoz Shah Tughlaq imposed jizya on them.

st.1: Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, called Mujaddid Alf-i-Sani, belonged to the Naqshbandi order.

x: All three statements are correct: Sirhindi was a Naqshbandi, he and Badauni criticised Akbar from an orthodox standpoint, and Mohsin Fani called Din-i-Ilahi a religion.
All three statements are correct: Shah Jahan moved the capital to Shahjahanabad in 1638-48, was confined in Agra Fort after 1658 with Jahanara nursing him, and died there in 1666.

st.1: Niccolao Manucci, a Venetian, wrote the Storia do Mogor.

x: All three statements are correct: Manucci wrote the Storia do Mogor, Tavernier traced the Koh-i-Noor to Kollur, and Bernier served Dara Shikoh and then Danishmand Khan.

st.2: The Maghi Mela is held at Sri Muktsar Sahib.

x: All three statements are correct: Hola Mohalla is linked with Anandpur Sahib, the Maghi Mela with Sri Muktsar Sahib, and the Akal Takht was built by Guru Hargobind in 1609.

st.1: Babur's memoir, the Baburnama (Tuzuk-i-Baburi), was written in Chagatai Turkish.

x: All three statements are correct: Babur wrote in Chagatai Turkish, Abdur Rahim Khan-i-Khana translated it into Persian, and Mutamid Khan continued Jahangir's memoir.

st.2: Breath control became vital in almost every Sufi order except the Chishtis.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: breath control was vital in almost every order except the Naqshbandis; the Chishtis adopted it.

st.2: The Portuguese obtained Bassein from Bahadur Shah of Gujarat in 1534.
st.4: Hooghly was granted to the Portuguese by a farman of Jahangir.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Hooghly was granted to the Portuguese by a farman of Akbar, not Jahangir.

st.3: Armagaon lies in present-day Tirupati district.

x: All four statements are correct: Armagaon (1626, Dugarajapatnam) was named after Armugam Mudali, lies in today's Tirupati district (old Nellore region), and the Visakhapatnam factory came in 1682.

st.3: An Indian sepoy could ordinarily rise no higher than the rank of Subedar.

x: All three statements are correct: the General Service Enlistment Act of 1856, the stopping of bhatta for Sindh and Punjab, and the Subedar ceiling for Indian sepoys.

st.2: It was read out by Lord Canning at a durbar in Allahabad.

x: All four statements are correct: Canning read the Proclamation at Allahabad; it addressed the Princes, Chiefs and Peoples of India, is called the Magna Carta of the Indian people and disclaimed further annexation.

st.2: He met Ranjit Singh at Rupar in 1831.

x: All three statements are correct: Sleeman was set against the Thugs, Bentinck met Ranjit Singh at Rupar in 1831 (the treaty of perpetual friendship was the 1809 Treaty of Amritsar), and he took over Mysore and annexed Coorg.

st.2: Sir William Jones founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal in 1784.

x: All three statements are correct: Hastings set up the Calcutta Madrasa in 1781, Jones founded the Asiatic Society in 1784 and Wilkins translated the Gita in 1785.

st.4: The Allahabad High Court was set up in 1866.

x: All four statements are correct: the CPC came in 1859, the IPC in 1860, the three Presidency High Courts in 1862 and the Allahabad High Court (first at Agra) in 1866.

All four statements are correct: Impey was the first Chief Justice at Calcutta (1774), the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council dates from 1833, the Federal Court from the 1935 Act, and Cornwallis set up four provincial courts of appeal.

st.2: B.R. Ambedkar rejected the term "Harijan".

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi took 'Harijan' from Narsi Mehta, Ambedkar rejected the term, and the weekly Harijan began at Poona on 11 February 1933.

st.3: Mahmud-ul-Hasan belonged to the Deoband school, not to the Aligarh Movement.

x: All three statements are correct: Hali, Mohsin-ul-Mulk, Chiragh Ali and Nazir Ahmad led the later Aligarh Movement, while Mahmud-ul-Hasan was a Deoband leader.

st.2: Aurobindo Ghosh was a member of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Aurobindo Ghosh was an Extremist leader of Bengal but not one of Lal-Bal-Pal.

st.2: At the Bombay Congress of 1915 Besant got the Congress to approve her Home Rule League scheme.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Bombay Congress of 1915 did not approve Besant's scheme; she was only allowed to start her league if the Congress did not act by September 1916.

st.3: "Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule" (December 1939) was written by Fazlul Haq.

x: All four statements are correct: the Pirpur Report (1938), the Sharif Report on Bihar (1939), Fazlul Haq's "Muslim Sufferings under Congress Rule" and the 'Hindu Raj' charge over Urdu.

st.1: The world's first Partition Museum (2017) is at the Town Hall, Lahore.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Partition Museum (2017) is at the Town Hall, Amritsar, not Lahore.

st.2: 'Gokhale: My Political Guru' was written by Gandhi.

x: All three statements are correct: 'Songs from Prison', 'Gokhale: My Political Guru' and 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth' are all Gandhi's.

st.2: After the operation J.N. Chaudhuri became the Military Governor of Hyderabad.

x: All three statements are correct: troops entered on 13 September 1948 and the Nizam ceased fire on 17 September; J.N. Chaudhuri became Military Governor (K.M. Munshi was the Agent-General); Razakar violence and the Standstill breach were causes.

st.1: Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae, which claimed Madras as an Andhra city, was written by T. Prakasam.

x: All three statements are correct: T. Prakasam wrote Chenna Nagaramu Andhra Nagaramae, Andhra Patrika popularised 'Andhra', and Deshabhimani was the only daily of British Andhra.

st.1: Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao, who presided at Kadapa in 1918, supported the province resolution there.

x: All three statements are correct: Nemali Pattabhi Rama Rao, who had opposed it in 1916, backed the province at Kadapa in 1918; Visakhapatnam (1915) demanded mother-tongue instruction; Nellore (1917) voted district-wise.

st.2: Krishna and Guntur were the keenest supporters of the separate province.

x: All three statements are correct: delta surplus went to Tamil areas, Krishna and Guntur were the keenest supporters (Rayalaseema and Nellore were lukewarm), and a Visakhapatnam port was an early demand.

All four statements are correct: the Andhra Congress Circle was sanctioned at Calcutta (1917), formed on 22 January 1918 with Konda Venkatappayya as secretary, and the Bezawada AICC (1921) launched the Tilak Swaraj Fund.

st.2: The Raja of Bobbili, Justice Party Chief Minister of Madras from 1932, opposed Andhra separation.

x: All three statements are correct: the Wardha CWC assured the deputation in 1938, the Raja of Bobbili opposed separation, and the 1945-46 manifesto promised linguistic units.

st.2: The Presidential Order of 1975 provided for local cadres and local reservation in public employment.

x: All three statements are correct: Article 371D came by the 32nd Amendment, the 1975 Presidential Order set up local cadres (the Telangana Regional Committee was a 1958 body), and Section 97 of the 2014 Act extended Article 371D.
Both statements are correct: the Patagandigudem plates are Ikshvaku and record a land grant for a Buddhist monastery.

st.2: Satavahana records mention 18 guilds.

x: All four statements are correct: a guild was headed by a Shreshthi, Satavahana records mention 18 guilds, guilds fixed quality and prices, and they later hardened into castes.

st.3: Its Sanskrit retelling, the Kathasaritsagara, is by Somadeva of Kashmir.

x: All three statements are correct: Gunadhya wrote in Paishachi after his bet with Sarvavarma, and the Kathasaritsagara is by Somadeva of Kashmir (not the Jain Somadeva Suri).

st.2: Sankarshana and Vasudeva, deities of the Bhagavata cult, are invoked in it.

x: All three statements are correct: Naganika's Naneghat record lists Satakarni I's sacrifices and invokes Sankarshana and Vasudeva along with Varuna and Yama.

st.3: She donated nine ayaka pillars.

x: All four statements are correct: Chamtisri, first woman donor and aunt of Virapurushadatta, rebuilt the Maha Chaitya in his 6th year with nine ayaka pillars and gave 170 dinari-masakas.

st.4: His sisters were Santisri (Chamtisri) and Harmyasri.

x: All four statements are correct: Santamula worshipped Virupakshapati and Mahasena, gave agraharas to northern Brahmins, performed the Vedic sacrifices, and had Santisri and Harmyasri as sisters (Bapisri and Chatisri were Virapurushadatta's queens).

st.3: He rebuilt the Maha Chaitya under Acharya Bhadanta Ananda.

x: All three statements are correct: Virapurushadatta was the only Ikshvaku Buddhist king, the 'Ashoka of the South', and the Maha Chaitya was rebuilt in his reign under Bhadanta Ananda (Nagarjuna was linked to the earlier Satavahana chaitya).

st.1: The Salar Jung Museum was opened in 1951.

x: All three statements are correct: the Salar Jung Museum opened in 1951 (by Nehru), houses the Veiled Rebecca, and the AP State Museum is now the Telangana State Museum.

st.3: K. Gopalachari held that they were Agnikula Kshatriyas.

x: All three statements are correct: the capital moved from Amarapuri to Denduluru, the Chikkulla plates came from Denduluru, and Gopalachari called them Agnikula Kshatriyas (most others: Brahmins).

st.2: He repelled the Rashtrakuta Krishna II at Koppam and Dharanikota.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhima I repelled Krishna II at Niravadyapura and Peruvanguru, not Koppam and Dharanikota.

st.4: He is hailed as Kavibrahma.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: 'Kavibrahma' is Tikkana's title, not Palkuriki Somanatha's.

st.2: The Karnam was the village accountant.

x: All three statements are correct: the Reddi village had 12 Ayagars paid in Manyam land or Mera, and the Karnam was the accountant.

st.2: Hussain Sagar was declared the UNWTO 'Heart of the World' in 2012.

x: All three statements are correct: Hyderabad was planned like Isfahan by Mir Momin, Hussain Sagar got the 'Heart of the World' tag in 2012, and the capital moved from Golconda in 1592.

st.3: His general Saluva Mangu, who killed the Madurai Sultan, received the title 'Parapakshi Saluva'.

x: All three statements are correct: Bukka I was Vedamarga Pratishthapaka, took Srisailam and Dupadu, and his general Saluva Mangu became 'Parapakshi Saluva'.

st.3: Purandaradasa, the father of Carnatic music, was a disciple of Vyasatirtha.

x: All four statements are correct: Timmarusu was later blinded, Vyasatirtha was the Madhva rajaguru and Purandaradasa's guru, and Babur called Krishnadevaraya the most powerful ruler.

st.2: Chand Bibi was married to Ali Adil Shah I of Bijapur.

x: All three statements are correct: Rama Raya took the Raichur doab in 1546-47, Chand Bibi married Ali Adil Shah I of Bijapur, and Bibi Jamal married Ibrahim Qutb Shah.

All three statements are correct: Mackenzie reached Amaravati in 1797 and became Surveyor General in 1815, 'Italian of the East' goes back to Nicolo de Conti, and Brown published Vemana's verses in 1829.

st.3: Viswanatha Satyanarayana won the first Telugu Jnanpith for Veyi Padagalu.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Viswanatha won the first Telugu Jnanpith for Ramayana Kalpavrukshamu, not Veyi Padagalu.
All three statements are correct: the Andhra Moderates echoed the drain theory, Anandacharlu attended the first INC session and Nyapathi Subbarao was a Rajahmundry lawyer.

st.4: T. Prakasam secured the release of the Tenali Bomb Case accused.

x: All four statements are correct: the Kotappakonda riots of February 1909, Chinnapa Reddy's death sentence, the Tenali accused, and T. Prakasam securing their release.

st.2: Governor Sri Prakasa invited C. Rajagopalachari to form the government.

x: Both statements are correct: the United Front chose Prakasam, but Governor Sri Prakasa invited Rajagopalachari.
All three statements are correct: Nehru ruled out Madras as capital, the capital had to be within Andhra, and some offices could stay in Madras for a time.
Both statements are correct: in June 2025 Tholu Bommalata and Burrakatha were flagged as near extinction, for lack of patronage and youth interest.

st.3: He was named Indian Film Personality of the Year at the Kolkata International Film Festival.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Indian Film Personality of the Year award (2022) came at IFFI Goa, not the Kolkata festival.

st.3: An inscription of Ananda on Sanchi's south torana links it to the Sunga king Pushyamitra.
st.4: Gupta temple architecture began under the Sungas.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Ananda's inscription links the torana to the Satavahana Satakarni II. Statement 4 is wrong: Gupta temple architecture did not begin under the Sungas.

st.3: Susharman, the last Kanva, was overthrown by the Satavahana Gautamiputra Satakarni.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Susharman was overthrown by the Satavahana Simuka, not Gautamiputra Satakarni.

st.3: Surkhi (brick-dust lime mortar) is first found in Kushana levels at Mathura.

x: All three statements are correct: the Shakas and Kushanas brought new dress, better cavalry, and surkhi is first found in Kushana levels at Mathura.

st.2: Roman gold flowed from the Tamil country to Rome in payment for Roman goods.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the direction is reversed; Roman gold coins flowed into the Tamil country in payment for Indian goods.

st.2: Tibetan sources call the five great monasteries together the Panchamahavihara.

x: All three statements are correct: Gopala's Odantapuri was a model for Tibet, Tibetan sources call the five the Panchamahavihara, and Ramapala's Jagaddala translated books into Tibetan.

st.1: The Durga temple has an apsidal plan with a circumambulatory passage.

x: All three statements are correct: the Durga temple is apsidal, Sastri called Aihole the cradle of temple architecture, and the Lad Khan temple has a flat roof with no shikhara.

st.1: Its Virupaksha temple was built to mark Vikramaditya II's victory over the Pallavas.

x: All four statements are correct: the Virupaksha temple marks the victory over the Pallavas, Pattadakal became a World Heritage Site in 1987, it was the Chalukya coronation site, and Nagara and Dravida temples stand side by side.

st.3: Quilon (Kollam), a centre of Arab and Chinese trade, is in Kerala.
st.4: Nagapattinam was the early capital of the Cholas.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the early Chola capital was Uraiyur (with Puhar as port-capital), not Nagapattinam.
Both statements are correct: Oxfam's 'Survival of the Richest' came out in January 2023 and found the bottom 50% held about 3% of India's wealth.

st.2: The Dr Ambedkar Scheme gives Rs 2.5 lakh to inter-caste couples even when neither spouse is a Dalit.
st.3: In July 2026 the Allahabad High Court held that the personal-law 'puberty' rule overrides the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the scheme gives Rs 2.5 lakh only when one spouse is a Dalit. Statement 3 is wrong: the High Court held that the Child Marriage Act overrides the personal-law puberty rule, not the reverse.

st.1: Andre Beteille did the fieldwork for 'Caste, Class and Power' in Sripuram, Tirunelveli.
st.2: Beteille found that caste, class and power coincide with one another.
st.4: According to Louis Dumont, the king stands at the top of the hierarchy, above the Brahman.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Sripuram is in Thanjavur. Statement 2 is wrong: Beteille found caste, class and power no longer coincide. Statement 4 is wrong: for Dumont the Brahman stands above the king.

st.2: The first order under Article 342(1) was made by Parliament as the Constitution (Scheduled Tribes) Order, 1950.
st.3: A single, identical list of Scheduled Tribes applies to the whole of India.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1950 Order was made by the President, not Parliament. Statement 3 is wrong: ST lists are State/UT-specific, not a single list for all India.

st.1: The National Policy for Empowerment of Women was adopted in 2001 by the National Commission for Women.
st.3: The Draft National Policy for Women, 2016 placed food security and nutrition under the economy.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 2001 policy was adopted by the Government of India, not by the NCW. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2016 draft placed food security and nutrition under health.

st.1: In August 2026 the Centre supported an income-based creamy layer in SC/ST quotas.
st.3: Jarnail Singh (2018) held that the creamy layer does not apply to SC/ST promotions.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: in August 2026 the Centre opposed an income-based creamy layer. Statement 3 is wrong: Jarnail Singh applied the creamy layer to SC/ST promotions.

st.3: Its demand for Greater Nagaland is an example of separatism within the Indian Union.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Greater Nagaland is an example of secessionism (out of India), not separatism within the Union.

st.2: Section 94 of the Act provides the backward-areas package.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the backward-areas package is in Section 46(2)-(3); Section 94 deals with tax incentives.

st.1: The Palermo Protocol (2000) supplements the UN Convention against Corruption.
st.2: India has not ratified the Palermo Protocol.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Protocol supplements the UN Convention against Transnational Organized Crime. Statement 2 is wrong: India ratified it in 2011.

st.4: Under Section 22, a child who makes a false complaint is also punishable.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: child marriage is not an offence under POCSO (the notes). Statement 4 is wrong: Section 22 punishes false complaints (except those in good faith) but no punishment is imposed on a child.

st.1: Denial of property, work and mobility to women is exclusion based on caste.
st.3: The term was coined by Amartya Sen in France in 1974.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: denial of property, work and mobility to women is exclusion based on gender. Statement 3 is wrong: the term was coined by René Lenoir.

st.1: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao is implemented under the Samarthya component of Mission Shakti.
st.2: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao provides direct benefit transfers to every girl child.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: BBBP falls under the Sambal component. Statement 2 is wrong: BBBP has no direct benefit transfer to girls.

st.1: ICDS was launched on 2 October 1975 on an experimental basis in 33 districts.
st.2: ICDS was universalised by an Act of Parliament.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: ICDS began in 33 blocks, not districts. Statement 2 is wrong: universalisation followed Supreme Court orders, not an Act.

st.1: PMJJBY gives a life cover of ₹2 lakh for accidental death only, at a premium of ₹436 a year.
st.4: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2007) gives life and disability cover to urban street vendors.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: PMJJBY covers death from any cause. Statement 4 is wrong: Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana covered rural landless households, not urban street vendors.

st.1: The National Human Rights Commission is set up under the PCR Act, 1955.
st.3: In Sukanya Shantha (2024), the Supreme Court upheld caste-based allocation of work in prison manuals.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NHRC is set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. Statement 3 is wrong: the Court struck down caste-based prison work as violating Article 17.

st.1: The Central Waqf Council is a constitutional body set up in 1964.
st.3: The Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 8 August 2024.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Central Waqf Council is a statutory body (1964), not a constitutional one. Statement 3 is wrong: the Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Lok Sabha.

st.2: The UAE sends India more remittances than the US.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the US, not the UAE, is the largest source of remittances to India.

st.3: Nauru, the newest member of the IMF, joined in 2021.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Nauru is not the newest member; Liechtenstein joined after it, as the 191st member in October 2024.

st.4: India took over the chair of BIMSTEC in April 2025.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: Bangladesh, not India, took over the BIMSTEC chair in April 2025 after the Bangkok Summit.

st.3: Its 'black list' is the list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring is the 'grey list'; the 'black list' is of high-risk jurisdictions subject to a call for action.

st.1: The Resistance Front (TRF) is a proxy of Jaish-e-Mohammed, not of LeT.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: The Resistance Front is a proxy of LeT, not of Jaish-e-Mohammed.

st.1: The National Register of Citizens (NRC) covers all usual residents of India.
st.3: Section 9 of the Aadhaar Act states that an Aadhaar number is proof of citizenship.
st.4: The Assam NRC's cut-off date was fixed by the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NRC covers only citizens; the NPR covers usual residents. Statement 3 is wrong: Section 9 says Aadhaar is not proof of citizenship. Statement 4 is wrong: the cut-off (24 March 1971) comes from the Assam Accord and Section 6A, not the CAA, 2019.

st.2: For a person born in India between 1 July 1987 and 2 December 2004, both parents must be Indian citizens.
st.3: A person born in India on or after 3 December 2004 is a citizen if one parent is a citizen, even if the other is an illegal migrant.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: for 1987-2004 births, one citizen parent is enough. Statement 3 is wrong: from 3 December 2004 both parents must be citizens, or one a citizen and the other not an illegal migrant.

st.2: Humanism is one of the grounds on which the freedom of religion may be restricted.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: humanism is not a ground; Article 25 is subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III provisions.

st.2: The President must revoke it if the Lok Sabha passes a resolution disapproving it by a special majority.
st.4: If the two Houses disagree, the proclamation may be approved at a joint sitting.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: each House must approve it separately. Statement 2 is wrong: a Lok Sabha disapproval resolution needs only a simple majority. Statement 4 is wrong: there is no joint sitting for an emergency proclamation.

st.1: The date 26 November 1949 mentioned in the Preamble is the date of commencement of the Constitution.
st.3: Before 2015, 26 November was observed as Republic Day.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: 26 November 1949 is the date of adoption, not commencement. Statement 3 is wrong: 26 November was National Law Day before it became Constitution Day in 2015; Republic Day is 26 January.

st.3: Jarnail Singh refused to apply the creamy layer principle to SC/ST promotions.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Jarnail Singh applied the creamy layer principle to SC/ST promotions.

st.2: India borrowed the concept from the Government of India Act, 1935.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Rule of Law was borrowed from the British Constitution, not the Government of India Act, 1935.

st.2: K.S. Puttaswamy (2017), decided by a nine-judge bench under CJI Dipak Misra, held privacy to be a Fundamental Right.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the nine-judge Puttaswamy bench was headed by CJI J.S. Khehar, not Dipak Misra.

st.2: The duty in Article 51A(i) also applies to resident foreigners.
st.3: The concept was taken from the Constitution of the USA.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Fundamental Duties apply only to citizens. Statement 3 is wrong: the concept was taken from the USSR, not the USA.

st.1: It was created by the First Amendment (1951), which also inserted Article 31C.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the First Amendment created the Ninth Schedule and inserted Articles 31A and 31B; Article 31C came by the 25th Amendment (1971).

st.1: Article 141 embodies stare decisis – the law declared by the Supreme Court binds all courts in India, including the Supreme Court itself.
st.3: In Ram Jawaya Kapur (1955), the Supreme Court held that India follows a rigid separation of powers.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Supreme Court is not bound by its own earlier decisions. Statement 3 is wrong: Ram Jawaya Kapur held India does not follow a rigid separation of powers.

st.2: Parliament is bound by the views of the State legislature to which the Bill is referred.
st.4: A Bill affecting a Union Territory must also be referred to the legislature of that Union Territory.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Parliament is not bound by the State legislature's views. Statement 4 is wrong: no such reference is needed for a Union Territory.

st.2: Delhi's three Rajya Sabha members are elected by the Municipal Corporation of Delhi.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Delhi's Rajya Sabha members are elected by the elected members of the Delhi Legislative Assembly, not the Municipal Corporation.

st.3: In the 1989 general election, Assam's 14 seats were polled along with the rest of the country.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in 1989 Assam's 14 seats were not polled, so only 529 seats went to the polls.

st.2: The Chairman votes in the first instance like other members.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Chairman does not vote in the first instance; he has only a casting vote in a tie.

st.2: No removal motion has ever been moved against Balram Jakhar.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a removal motion was moved against Balram Jakhar in 1987 (Hukam Singh faced one in 1966).

st.1: It can be moved in either House of Parliament.
st.4: More than one adjournment motion may be taken up at a sitting.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the adjournment motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha. Statement 4 is wrong: not more than one adjournment motion can be taken up at a sitting.

st.1: It is expressly provided for in Article 75(3) of the Constitution.
st.2: It can be moved in either House of Parliament.
st.4: It must state the reasons for which it is moved.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 75(3) lays down collective responsibility, not the motion itself. Statement 2 is wrong: it can be moved only in the Lok Sabha. Statement 4 is wrong: a no-confidence motion need not state reasons.

st.2: Under Rajya Sabha Rule 255, the Chairman may direct a member to withdraw for the rest of the session.
st.3: Rajya Sabha Rule 256 provides for automatic suspension of a member without any motion of the House.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under Rule 255 the withdrawal is for the rest of the day. Statement 3 is wrong: suspension under Rule 256 needs a motion of the House.

st.1: The Monsoon Session from 17 August 2026 was summoned by the Speaker under Article 174(1).
st.2: Biometric attendance of MLAs was made mandatory from the Monsoon Session that began on 17 August 2026.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Monsoon Session was summoned by the Governor, not the Speaker, under Article 174(1). Statement 2 is wrong: biometric attendance became mandatory from the Budget Session of 11 February 2026.

All four statements are correct: the six weeks run from the later reassembly, disapproval by both Houses ends an ordinance, Article 85 caps the gap at six months, and 60 days' unexcused absence can vacate a seat.

st.2: In a hung Assembly, the Constitution lays down detailed criteria for the Governor's choice of Chief Minister.
st.3: Under the Sarkaria-Punchhi order of preference, a post-poll coalition is invited before the single largest party with the support of others.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Constitution lays down no criteria for the Governor's choice. Statement 3 is wrong: the single largest party with others' support comes before a post-poll coalition.

st.2: He has the right to vote in the State Legislature under Article 177.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under Article 177 the Advocate General may speak in the Legislature but has no right to vote.

st.1: Part XIV-A was inserted by the 42nd Amendment, 1976 on the advice of the Sarkaria Commission.
st.3: Tribunal chairpersons generally get the status of a Supreme Court judge.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Part XIV-A followed the Swaran Singh Committee, not the Sarkaria Commission. Statement 3 is wrong: tribunal chairpersons generally get the status of a High Court judge.

st.2: According to Laxmikanth, the Central Services violate the principle of federalism.
st.3: Vesting residuary power in Parliament is, according to Laxmikanth, violative of federalism.
st.4: The President taking over a State's administration under the emergency provisions is not violative of federalism.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: it is the All India Services that Laxmikanth says violate federalism, not the Central Services. Statement 3 is wrong: residuary power with Parliament is not violative. Statement 4 is wrong: the President taking over a State under emergency is violative.

st.1: Article 256 requires the executive power of every State to be exercised so as to ensure compliance only with laws made by its own Legislature.
st.3: Under Article 257, the Union may direct a State on the maintenance of public order.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: Article 256 requires compliance with laws made by Parliament. Statement 3 is wrong: Article 257 directions concern means of communication and railways, not public order.

st.2: Its Standing Committee is chaired by the Prime Minister.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Standing Committee is chaired by the Union Home Minister; the Prime Minister chairs the Council itself.

st.1: When the office of the Chairman of a Public Service Commission is vacant, the senior-most member automatically acts as Chairman.
st.2: The age limit of UPSC members was raised from 60 to 62 by the 41st Amendment, 1976.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: an acting Chairman is appointed by the President or Governor; the senior member does not act automatically. Statement 2 is wrong: the 41st Amendment raised the age of State PSC members, not UPSC members.

st.1: Its advice is binding on the government.
st.2: Consultation with the UPSC is mandatory, and action taken without consulting it is invalid.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: UPSC advice is only advisory. Statement 2 is wrong: action taken without consulting the UPSC is not invalid.

st.3: Members of the UPSC can be removed either by the Governor or by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry.
st.4: Members of the National Commission for Backward Classes are appointed by the Prime Minister.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: UPSC members are removed only by the President. Statement 4 is wrong: NCBC members are appointed by the President, not the Prime Minister.

st.2: In India every human right is also a Fundamental Right.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: not every human right is a Fundamental Right in India.

st.2: The ICCPR entered into force before the ICESCR.
st.3: India acceded to both Covenants in 1979 and has also ratified the ICCPR First Optional Protocol.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the ICESCR came into force first (January 1976), the ICCPR in March 1976. Statement 3 is wrong: India has not signed the First Optional Protocol.

st.2: It seeks to make all information public, without any exemption.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Act harmonises transparency with confidentiality and has exemptions.

st.2: Karnataka set up its Lokayukta, with its own Lokayukta Police wing, under a law made by Parliament.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Karnataka's Lokayukta was set up under the State's own Karnataka Lokayukta Act, 1984, not a law of Parliament.

st.1: Under Section 3 of the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, an aggrieved State complains directly to the Supreme Court.
st.3: The Supreme Court's original jurisdiction under Article 131 covers such water disputes.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: under Section 3 the State asks the Central Government to refer the dispute to a tribunal. Statement 3 is wrong: such disputes are kept out of Article 131 jurisdiction.

st.3: The Republican Party of India was formed during Dr B.R. Ambedkar's lifetime.
st.4: The Samajwadi Party, founded at Lucknow in 1992, is a recognised national party.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the RPI was formed in 1957, after Ambedkar's death. Statement 4 is wrong: the Samajwadi Party is a State party, not a national party.

st.3: According to ADR, the share of Lok Sabha MPs facing serious criminal charges fell between 2009 and 2024.
st.4: The special courts for cases against MPs and MLAs were set up by an Act of Parliament.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the share rose from 14% (2009) to 31% (2024). Statement 4 is wrong: the 12 special courts came on Supreme Court directions, not an Act.

All three statements are correct: proxy 'sarpanch pati' behaviour falls in a second term, the Sushil Kumar committee suggested exemplary penalties, and the Sashakt Panchayat-Netri Abhiyan builds women leaders.

st.2: The basic-to-performance grant ratio of 80:20 applied to Panchayats.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 80:20 ratio applied to Municipalities; Panchayats had 90:10.

st.3: Under the Atmanirbhar Panchayat Program, a Gram Panchayat must have own revenue of at least Rs 1 crore.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: a Gram Panchayat needs own revenue of Rs 50 lakh; Rs 1 crore is the Block threshold.

st.2: The Unified Payments Interface (UPI), on which BHIM is built, was developed by the Reserve Bank of India.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: UPI was developed by the NPCI, not the RBI.

st.3: UDAN provides free air travel to common people on regional routes.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: UDAN does not give free travel; it caps fares with viability gap funding.

st.2: Justice C.K. Prasad preceded Justice Markandey Katju as Chairman.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Katju (2011-14) came first; C.K. Prasad followed him (2014-22).

st.3: Galeru-Nagari is a Godavari-based project.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Galeru-Nagari is a Krishna-based project, not Godavari-based.

st.3: India's per capita availability is below 1,700 cubic metres, making it water-stressed.

x: All three statements are correct: below 1,700 m3 is water-stressed, below 1,000 m3 water-scarce, and India is water-stressed but not yet water-scarce.

st.2: Vizhinjam in Kerala is India's first deep-water transhipment port.

x: All three statements are correct: Cochin airport was the first PPP and fully solar airport, Vizhinjam (Kerala) is the first deep-water transhipment port, and Navi Mumbai airport opened on 25 December 2025.

st.3: The Infant Mortality Rate is expressed per 1,000 live births.

x: All three statements are correct: MMR is per 1,00,000 live births, IMR per 1,000 live births, and the dependency ratio is the 0-14 plus 65+ population over the 15-64 population.

st.3: Reduction of adult obesity is one of its four headline targets along with stunting, underweight and anaemia.
st.4: The POSHAN Tracker is used for real-time monitoring of school mid-day meals.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the targets are stunting, undernutrition, anaemia and low birth weight, not adult obesity. Statement 4 is wrong: the POSHAN Tracker monitors Anganwadi services.

st.1: The National Infrastructure Pipeline was launched in December 2019 as part of PM Gati Shakti.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the NIP (December 2019) came before PM Gati Shakti, which was launched in October 2021.

st.3: Private consumption grew faster than real gross fixed capital formation.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: private consumption grew 7.1%, slower than real GFCF (11.9%).

st.1: Like the Clark-Fisher sequence, India moved from agriculture to manufacturing and then to services.
st.3: An increase in the working population is an adverse effect of population growth.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: India skipped a manufacturing-led stage. Statement 3 is wrong: a larger working population is not an adverse effect of population growth.
Both statements are correct: the rupee was devalued by 36.5% on 6 June 1966, and a Plan Holiday followed the Third Plan.

st.2: Scheduled Castes had the highest poverty ratio among social groups.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Scheduled Tribes, not Scheduled Castes, had the highest poverty ratio.

st.2: No liberalisation at all took place under Rajiv Gandhi.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: some liberalisation did take place under Rajiv Gandhi (broad-banding, easier imports).

st.2: Expanding the list of industries reserved for the public sector
st.3: FDI through the automatic route in all sectors
st.4: Full capital account convertibility

x: Only 1 was part of the 1991 policy. 2 is wrong: the reserved list for the public sector was cut, not expanded. 3 is wrong: the automatic route covered only listed industries, not all sectors. 4 is wrong: full capital account convertibility was never adopted.

st.1: Cesses and surcharges, which touched ₹13.5 per ₹100 of Central tax in 2021-22, form part of the divisible pool.
st.2: Effective devolution to States is above the headline 41% of gross tax revenue.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: cesses and surcharges are kept out of the divisible pool. Statement 2 is wrong: effective devolution is only about 30-32%, below the headline 41%.

st.3: In the Fiscal Health Index 2026 (FY 2023-24), Odisha was first again and Andhra Pradesh was last.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: in FHI 2026 Odisha was first and Punjab last; Andhra Pradesh was 17th.

st.1: M2 is a measure of broad money.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: M2 is narrow money; M3 is broad money.

st.3: NEFT, like RTGS, settles each transaction on a real-time gross basis.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: NEFT settles in batches on a deferred net basis; only RTGS is real-time gross.

st.2: The Supreme Court upheld the 2016 demonetisation by a 4:1 majority in 2023, with Justice S. Abdul Nazeer dissenting.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the dissent was by Justice B.V. Nagarathna; Justice Abdul Nazeer headed the bench.

st.2: Primary Agricultural Credit Societies come under the direct control of the RBI.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PACS come under the State Registrars of Cooperative Societies, not the RBI.

st.2: Their number came down to 43 under One State-One RRB.
st.3: Under One State-One RRB, the RBI notified the amalgamation of 26 RRBs, leaving 28.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: 43 was the count after the 2020-21 round; One State-One RRB left 28. Statement 3 is wrong: the amalgamation (effective 1 May 2025) was notified by the Central Government under the RRB Act, not the RBI.

st.1: The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 applies only after a person has been convicted by a court.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Act applies to persons with a warrant against them who have left India, for ₹100 crore and above; no conviction is needed.

st.4: Food and beverages carry a larger weight in it than in the 2012-based series.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: food and beverages weigh 36.75% in the new series, less than in the 2012 series.

st.1: In the 2026-27 BE, gross tax revenue is projected to grow faster than nominal GDP.
st.2: In the 2026-27 BE, the buoyancy of indirect taxes (1.1) exceeds that of direct taxes (0.3).

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: gross buoyancy is 0.8, so tax revenue grows slower than GDP. Statement 2 is wrong: direct taxes (1.1) are more buoyant than indirect taxes (0.3).

st.1: UTGST is levied on intra-UT supplies in Union Territories with a legislature.
st.3: The States administer and collect IGST.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: UTGST is levied in UTs without a legislature. Statement 3 is wrong: the Centre collects CGST and IGST.

st.2: Cut motions are moved at the stage of general discussion on the Budget.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: cut motions are moved at the voting on Demands for Grants, not the general discussion.

st.1: Since April 2020, FDI from a country sharing a land border with India has been barred altogether.
st.2: It covers Sri Lanka but not Bhutan.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: such FDI is allowed, but through the Government route. Statement 2 is wrong: Bhutan is covered and Sri Lanka, with no land border, is not.
Both statements are correct: 100% FDI is allowed under the automatic route in the marketplace model, and from July 2026 the inventory model is allowed for exporting domestically made goods.
Both statements are correct: in 2010-11 ST holdings were larger and SC holdings smaller than the all-groups average.

st.4: GM mustard DMH-11 has been under a moratorium since 2010.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the 2010 moratorium was on Bt brinjal; GM mustard DMH-11 was cleared for environmental release in 2022.

st.1: The FCI advises the MSP and the CACP procures wheat and rice.
st.3: The strategic reserve of 5 million tonnes is counted within the operational buffer stocks.
st.4: Under the Open Market Sale Scheme, NAFED sells surplus central-pool grain at predetermined prices.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the CACP advises the MSP and the FCI procures. Statement 3 is wrong: the strategic reserve is held above operational stocks. Statement 4 is wrong: the FCI, not NAFED, sells under OMSS.

st.3: In oilseeds, groundnut is the one crop whose Indian yield is below the world average while the others are above it.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: groundnut is the exception whose yield is above the world average.

st.2: The Pulses Conclave 2020, a biennial global pulses conference, was held in Madhya Pradesh.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Pulses Conclave 2020 was held in Maharashtra, not Madhya Pradesh.

st.2: It aimed to double farmers' income in nominal terms, with 2015-16 as base and 2022 as target.
st.3: It identified seven sources of income growth, including a shift from non-farm to farm jobs.
st.4: It shifted the policy focus from income to production.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the target was real (not nominal) income. Statement 3 is wrong: the shift was from farm to non-farm jobs. Statement 4 is wrong: it shifted focus from production to income.

st.1: The fertiliser subsidy is the largest subsidy of the Union Government, ahead of the food subsidy.
st.4: The National Investment Policy for Urea-2026 aims to add 10 MT of DAP capacity.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: fertiliser subsidy is the second largest, after food. Statement 4 is wrong: the 10 MT is urea capacity, not DAP.

st.2: The Fourth Amendment (1955) inserted the Ninth Schedule.
st.3: The Seventeenth Amendment (1964) was challenged in Kesavananda Bharati.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ninth Schedule came by the First Amendment; the Fourth widened Article 31A. Statement 3 is wrong: the 17th Amendment was challenged in Golaknath.

st.1: It regulates agricultural markets under State APMC laws.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the FCI does not regulate markets; APMCs are under State laws.

st.2: In the 2011-12 use-based classification, capital goods had the highest weight.
st.4: Gas supply, water supply, sewerage and waste management have been dropped in the new series.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: primary goods, not capital goods, had the highest weight. Statement 4 is wrong: these sectors were added, not dropped.

st.1: Manufacturing is the largest contributor to AP's GSDP.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: manufacturing contributes only about 11% of AP's GSDP.

st.3: AP leads India in fruit production but not in tobacco exports.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: AP also leads in tobacco exports, with about 67% of India's.

st.2: Agriculture and allied was the fastest-growing sector.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: services (10.67%) were the fastest-growing sector, not agriculture.

st.1: Public Debt liabilities of the undivided State were apportioned on the basis of area.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: debt was apportioned by population ratio, not area.
All three statements are correct: own tax was about 45% of revenue receipts in 2015-16, about 48% of the estimate was collected by November 2025, and non-tax revenue was under one-fifth of BE.

st.2: Thalliki Vandanam gets more than NTR Bharosa Pension.
st.3: Annadata Sukhibhava, a fully State-funded scheme with no PM-Kisan share, gets ₹6,600 crore.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: NTR Bharosa Pension is the highest; Thalliki Vandanam gets ₹8,456 crore. Statement 3 is wrong: Annadata Sukhibhava is run with PM-Kisan.

st.3: VAT on diesel is higher than VAT on petrol.
st.4: In December 2025 AP's fuel was the cheapest in India.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: VAT is 31% on petrol and 22.25% on diesel. Statement 4 is wrong: AP's fuel was the costliest in India.

st.2: AP Budget 2026-27 shows a revenue surplus.
st.3: The fiscal deficit of 3.8% of GSDP is within the 3% norm.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: there is a revenue deficit of ₹22,003 crore (1.1% of GSDP). Statement 3 is wrong: 3.8% exceeds the 3% norm.

st.2: Funds flow through State IFMIS and PFMS, bypassing RBI e-Kuber.
st.3: It covers 28 States but no Union Territories.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: funds flow through State IFMIS, RBI e-Kuber and PFMS. Statement 3 is wrong: it covers 28 States and 3 UTs (66 CSS).

st.2: The 16th Finance Commission wants CSS delinked from outcomes.
st.4: CS/CSS will continue after 31 March 2026 without any fresh appraisal.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the 16th FC wants CSS outcome-linked. Statement 4 is wrong: a new 5-year appraisal cycle begins on 1 April 2026.

st.1: The Godavari River Management Board has its headquarters in Andhra Pradesh.
st.2: The river management boards were to be set up by the two States within 60 days under Section 85.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Godavari board is headquartered in Telangana (Hyderabad). Statement 2 is wrong: the boards were to be set up by the Central Government.

st.1: The Sheela Bhide Committee recommended division of most Schedule X institutions; its term expired in August 2015 and the Centre revived it.
st.2: The committee for the partition of the 1953 Andhra State was chaired by Fazl Ali.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Sheela Bhide Committee dealt with Schedule IX bodies, not Schedule X institutions. Statement 2 is wrong: the 1953 partition committee was chaired by Justice K.N. Wanchoo, not Fazl Ali.

st.1: HUDCO and NABARD are external agencies, not domestic lenders.
st.2: The New Development Bank is a bilateral lender.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: HUDCO and NABARD are domestic lenders. Statement 2 is wrong: the New Development Bank is a multilateral lender.

st.1: The 10 fishing harbours are being built under Sagarmala.
st.2: The aqua-power tariff is Rs 1.50 per unit for all aqua farms, whatever their size or zone.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 10 fishing harbours are built under PMMSY, not Sagarmala. Statement 2 is wrong: Rs 1.50 applies only to farms up to 10 acres in notified zones.

st.2: Rythu Seva Kendras are run by the Union Ministry of Agriculture.
st.3: The farmers' Integrated Call Centre is located at Visakhapatnam.
st.4: Rythu Seva Kendras issue industrial licences along with soil testing and e-Panta.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Kendras are run by the AP government. Statement 3 is wrong: the Integrated Call Centre is at Gannavaram (toll-free 155251). Statement 4 is wrong: the Kendras do not issue industrial licences.

st.2: Sugarcane is included.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: sugarcane is not among the 11 productivity crops.

st.2: The KRMB and GRMB operate under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the KRMB and GRMB were set up under the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014, not the 1956 Act.

st.3: Innovation and extension, including the Rashtriya Gokul Mission

x: 1 and 2 are sub-schemes of the National Livestock Mission. 3 is wrong: livestock insurance comes under innovation and extension, but the Rashtriya Gokul Mission is a separate scheme.

st.2: Land-conversion fee is not reimbursed.
st.3: De-carbonisation support is not among the standard incentives.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: land-conversion fee is reimbursed 100%. Statement 3 is wrong: de-carbonisation support of up to 6% of FCI is a standard incentive.

st.2: Amaravati-Visakhapatnam is one of these seven growth connectors.
st.4: The Nagpur-Vijayawada expressway was dropped in January 2026.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Amaravati-Visakhapatnam is not one of the seven corridors. Statement 4 is wrong: the Nagpur-Vijayawada expressway was fast-tracked, not dropped, in January 2026.

st.1: The Cauvery basin around Kakinada and Konaseema is AP's oil and gas hub.
st.2: APGIC's equity is held 51% by APGENCO and 49% by APIIC.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the hub around Kakinada and Konaseema is the KG basin. Statement 2 is wrong: APGIC is APIIC 51% and APGENCO 49%.

st.2: It gives industry status only to Mega and Ultra Mega tourism projects.
st.3: It aims to place AP among the world's top three tourist destinations.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: industry status is given across all segments; Mega and Ultra Mega projects get tailor-made packages. Statement 3 is wrong: the aim is India's top three destinations.

st.2: The Ratan Tata Innovation Hub (August 2025) has its hub at Visakhapatnam.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub has its hub at Amaravati, not Visakhapatnam.

st.1: The Coal Controller's Organisation, headquartered at Kolkata, conducts coal block auctions.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: coal block auctions are run by the Nominated Authority, not the Coal Controller's Organisation.

st.4: The magnetic field is generated by the solid inner core.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is wrong: the magnetic field is generated in the liquid outer core, not the solid inner core.

st.2: The Tropic of Cancer passes through Iran.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Tropic of Cancer does not pass through Iran.

st.2: The core accounts for a larger share of the Earth's volume than the mantle.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the mantle (about 83%) is far larger than the core (about 16%) by volume.

st.3: Diorite is an extrusive rock formed by the quick cooling of lava.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: FCRA regulates, not bans, foreign donations. Statement 3 is wrong: transfer of foreign contribution to other NGOs is barred.

st.2: It was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.

x: All three statements are correct: the Cabinet decision to protect the National Song, its composition by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, and West Bengal's madrasa rule.

st.1: The first complete (synchronous) Census of India was held under Lord Mayo.
st.3: Sand artist Sudarsan Pattnaik is the Registrar General of India.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the first synchronous Census came in 1881 under Lord Ripon; Mayo's 1872 Census was not synchronous. Statement 3 is wrong: Pattnaik is Census 2027's brand ambassador, not the Registrar General.

st.2: Free biodegradable sanitary pads were directed for all women, not only schoolgirls.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the direction is for girls in Classes 6–12.

st.2: Online social games are banned along with online money games.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: online social games are promoted, not banned.

st.2: A State Waqf Board may have a non-Muslim majority.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: a State Waqf Board may have at most 3 non-Muslims out of 11.

st.3: Justice Sundresh held that an absolute bar on such recruitment violates Article 14.

x: All four statements are correct: the Gavai Bench allowed direct recruitment of serving officers, overruled the two cases, Justice Sundresh found the bar violates Article 14, and 7 years combined with a minimum age of 35 apply.

st.3: It allows a one-time restoration of the resolution process after the liquidation order is passed.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the Act does not provide for restoring the resolution process after a liquidation order.

st.2: Salaya, a tidal port and boat-repair hub, lies on the Gulf of Khambhat.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Salaya lies on the Gulf of Kutch, not the Gulf of Khambhat.
Both statements are correct: the first ASISSE (2024–25) covers about 21 lakh enterprises, and PAIMANA replaced the 2006 OCMS.

st.3: The Foreign Asset Disclosure Scheme is a one-time scheme meant for large corporate taxpayers.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the scheme is meant for small taxpayers, not large corporates.

st.2: It is a single new scheme that replaces 36 existing schemes.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: PM-DDKY converges 36 schemes of 11 Ministries over six years (2025-26 to 2030-31); it does not replace them.

st.2: The T3 approach became T4 by adding 'Trace' to Test, Treat and Talk.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: T3 became T4 by adding 'Track', not 'Trace'.

st.2: Its Price Deficiency Payment Scheme pays the gap between MSP and the sale price along with physical procurement.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: under PDPS the gap is paid without physical procurement.

st.1: It gives ₹6,000 a year to every farmer, including income-tax payers.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: income-tax payers are excluded; eligible farmers get ₹6,000 in three instalments.

st.3: The Centre itself deletes the ineligible ration cards.
st.4: Four-wheeler owners formed the largest flagged category.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the States, not the Centre, delete ineligible cards. Statement 4 is wrong: income-tax payers (94.71 lakh) were the largest category.

st.3: It gives collateral-free loans at the market rate of interest.
st.4: It gives a toolkit incentive of ₹15,000 in cash.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: loans (up to ₹3 lakh) are at a concessional 5%. Statement 4 is wrong: the ₹15,000 toolkit incentive is given as an e-voucher, not cash.

st.2: The recommendations of the Law Commission are binding on the Union Government.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Law Commission recommendations are not binding.

st.1: It raised the States' share of the divisible pool above 41%.

x: Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the 16th FC kept the States' share at 41%.

st.1: It was set up in 1969 by the Kerala government to study Centre-State relations.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the Rajamannar Committee was set up by the Tamil Nadu government, not Kerala.

st.2: The K. Radhakrishnan Committee examined police action in the NEET protests.
st.3: The National Testing Agency is a statutory body set up by an Act of Parliament.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Radhakrishnan Committee dealt with exam reform, not police action. Statement 3 is wrong: the NTA is a registered society, not a statutory body.

st.2: It recommended partial State funding of elections, in kind, for recognised parties.

x: All three statements are correct: the eight-member Indrajit Gupta committee backed partial State funding in kind for recognised parties, and the Kelkar Committee reported in November 2015.

st.1: The international basis of GI protection is the WTO's GATS agreement.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the international basis of GI protection is TRIPS, not GATS.

st.2: India's agricultural exports grew at a CAGR of about 12% during 2020-2025.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: agricultural exports grew at a CAGR of about 8.2%; about 12% is their share of core exports.

st.1: The nodal ministry for the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is the MoEFCC.
st.4: The Adi Karmayogi Abhiyan is run by the Ministry of Rural Development.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: the nodal ministry for the FRA is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Statement 4 is wrong: Adi Karmayogi is a Tribal Affairs programme.

st.1: Atmospheric CO₂ fell in 2024 for the first time since 1957.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: CO₂ rose to a record (about 424 ppm) in 2024.

st.2: It adopted the Fifth Strategic Plan and the Ankara Declaration.
st.4: Kasane-Kazungula, one of the new Ramsar Wetland Cities, is in Zambia.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: COP15 adopted the Fifth Strategic Plan (2025–2034) with the Victoria Falls Declaration. Statement 4 is wrong: Kasane-Kazungula is in Botswana.

st.2: It declared cricket a priority sport.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: badminton, not cricket, was declared a priority sport.

st.3: An agreement was made with IIT Hyderabad for IIT and NEET coaching.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: the coaching agreement is with IIT Madras, not IIT Hyderabad.

st.2: Polavaram and Markapuram districts were both carved out of Kurnool district.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Markapuram was carved from Prakasam and Polavaram from the Godavari agency areas, not from Kurnool.
All three statements are correct: Naidu was sworn in for the 4th time on 12 June 2024 by Governor Abdul Nazeer, and Amaravati is the capital under the 2026 Amendment Act.

st.2: Coringa WLS, established in 1978, is India's second-largest mangrove forest after Bhitarkanika.
st.3: The Olive Ridley is listed as Endangered by the IUCN.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Coringa is second after the Sundarbans, not Bhitarkanika. Statement 3 is wrong: the Olive Ridley is Vulnerable.

st.2: Online examinations to be expanded through private online centres.
st.3: 'Decayed teeth' to remain a disqualification for uniformed posts.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: exams are to be offline, because of fraud in private online centres. Statement 3 is wrong: 'decayed teeth' is to be removed as a disqualification.

st.2: Andhra Pradesh's mango exports are mainly of the Alphonso variety.
st.3: APEDA, a statutory body under the APEDA Act 1985, is headquartered in Mumbai.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: AP exports Banganapalli, Benishan and small Rasalu, about 8-10% of India's mango exports. Statement 3 is wrong: APEDA is headquartered in New Delhi.

st.3: Kerala ranked 1st with a score of 766.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Chandigarh ranked 1st with 766, not Kerala.

st.2: Orange (41–44°C) on the card means 'Extreme Danger'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong: orange (41–44°C) means 'Be Prepared'; red (45°C+) is 'Extreme Danger'.

st.2: Among the erstwhile districts, East Godavari ranked first.
st.4: All southern States, including Kerala, were in the top 10.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Visakhapatnam ranked first among erstwhile districts. Statement 4 is wrong: not all southern States were in the top 10.

st.2: The award was received on behalf of Andhra Pradesh by the AP Pollution Control Board.

x: Statements 1, 3 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the award was received by NREDCAP, not the AP Pollution Control Board.

st.2: The Tummalapalle lithium-gallium surveys are being carried out by the Geological Survey of India alone.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the surveys are under an AP-CSIR-NGRI pact (lithium up to 1,000 ppm, gallium up to 250 ppm).

st.2: Under the MMDR Act, 1957, sand is a major mineral regulated by the Centre.
st.3: The Sustainable Sand Mining Management Guidelines, 2016, which made the District Survey Report mandatory, were issued by the Ministry of Mines.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: sand is a minor mineral regulated by the States. Statement 3 is wrong: the 2016 guidelines were issued by the MoEFCC.

st.3: Racha Aribarg, who visited Sri City, is the Consul General of Malaysia in Chennai.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: Racha Aribarg is the Consul General of Thailand, not Malaysia.

st.2: AP's Korea roadshow ahead of the 31st summit (July 2026) was led by Pawan Kalyan.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Korea roadshow was led by Nara Lokesh, not Pawan Kalyan.
Both statements are correct: the Adani pumped storage project is in Kadapa, and a 1,344 MW project is under study.

st.2: Its four divisions are Guntakal, Guntur, Vijayawada and Rajahmundry.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the fourth division is Visakhapatnam (Waltair), not Rajahmundry.

st.3: KOHA, the subject of a workshop there, is an open-source Learning Management System.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: KOHA is an open-source Integrated Library System, not a Learning Management System.

st.3: She succeeded Justice Dhiraj Singh Thakur on transfer from the Delhi High Court.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is wrong: she came on transfer from the Punjab and Haryana High Court, not Delhi.

st.2: The Manjira is a left-bank tributary of the Godavari.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: the Manjira is a right-bank tributary.

st.2: It is being developed under the HRIDAY scheme.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kangundi is under Swarna Kuppam, not HRIDAY.

st.2: SFURTI, which benefited AP artisans, is a scheme of the Ministry of Textiles.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: SFURTI is an MSME Ministry scheme; it benefited 8,492 AP artisans.

st.1: Dr G. Satish Reddy, a former ISRO Chairman, became Advisor for Aerospace and Defence to the AP government.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 1 is wrong: G. Satish Reddy is a former DRDO Chairman, not ISRO.

st.2: Kondapalli toys are made of Ankudu wood.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Statement 2 is wrong: Kondapalli toys use Tella Poniki wood; Ankudu is used for Etikoppaka toys.
